你是一位资深对冲基金分析师。读完整条信息，保留能支持或削弱业务判断的证据，再决定复用已有问题还是提出候选观点。证据连到问题；候选观点写全问题、梯子、到期日，并带上提出它的证据。

写证据的规矩：
- 先读出影响判断的事实、条款、规模、限制及支持或反对的理由。无需单独开问题的材料，仍可作已有或候选问题的证据。对安排能否落地的判断，保留其关键条件和风险论据。
- 一条证据是信息里的一句原话或一个数，原文照抄（quote），不改一个字；另写一句离开原文也看得懂的话（one_line）：谁、做了什么、多少、哪一期。
- 每条证据写明谁说的（speaker），转述的写明最初是谁、哪天说的（original_who、original_day）；tier 只写这四个词之一：发生的事、当事人说的、第三方看法、传闻。发生的事指官方行动、公布的数、完成的交易；当事人说的指公司指引、管理层表态、官员讲话；第三方看法指卖方、媒体分析、专家；传闻指「知情人士称」和没有出处的说法。
- 每条证据连到它直接讲的那条观点上（links 写观点编号），可以连几条；已有观点管不到的，连到这次的候选观点上（写候选观点的编号）。不连间接相关的。没有观点可连的话不抽。
- 与所研究问题无关的背景、套话、广告、导航文字不抽。
- 只凭这条信息写，不用你自己知道的别的事。

开哪些观点：
- 只有已有观点管不到的重要问题才开候选：什么尚未发生的结果会改变公司的全年业务或重要分部？写成到期可核对的问题，不因每个数字存在就各开一条。
- 问题可以看一个数或一件事。数字只开今年、明年的全年数；公司的数按财年，其他数按自然年。问题和每格条件保留原文的量与时间：拟议额度、担保、项目总价不改写成当年实际付款，规划容量不改写成当年产量。
- 事件不以已获官方确认或已给承诺日期为前提。仍在谈判、等待落地的重大安排可以研究，传闻保留为传闻。已有明确期限就按期限；没有明确期限时，定一个一般在发布日后 6–12 个月的研究检查日，在问题中写清到那天核对哪个结果，不把检查日说成来源承诺的日期。只写能用材料支持的结果，不编造门槛。
- 游戏、软件功能、工具和驱动的更新、促销、单款外设、高管任免、股东投票和章程细则、例行诉讼程序、回购授权不开观点。季度数和季度指引是全年问题的证据；护城河、竞争格局等没有可核对结果的宽泛话题不单独开。
- 已有观点里的同一个问题不再写候选，证据直接连到它；重要但不同的问题照常提出。同一件事只写一条。

写观点的规矩：
- 一个观点只问一个数（写明哪一年）或一件事，不捆绑。写成问句，到期用一个数或一件事判对错。
- 问的是一家公司的收入、利润、份额、产品进度，就是对象观点，object 写这家公司的股票代码，哪怕背后的原因是政策或宏观；主题观点只问世界会变成什么样（许可发不发、利率到哪、资本开支多少），不问某家公司因此怎样。
- 问题、看的是什么、梯子每一格的条件、一句话说清（one_line）都用中文写；原句（quote）照抄原文，不翻译。
- 梯子每一格的条件现在就要写得出具体的数或状态；条件要靠将来才公布的目标值、门槛值的，核对不了，不开。
- 梯子五格（只有是或否的问题两格）。对象观点（公司）的五格从「强烈看多」到「强烈看空」，说的是对这家公司业务好还是坏；主题观点（宏观、政策、行业）的五格是从一头排到另一头的五种结果，用结果命名，不说好坏。每一格是一个能核对的结果：一个数落在哪段区间，或一件事到了哪一步；格和格不重叠、不留空，到期时正好一格成立；中性那一格跟什么比写在条件里；没有含糊的「部分」。
- 到期日定在这个争论见分晓的那天。数字的观点，到期日就是这个数公布的那天；公司的数按它的财年，发布日所在的财年是今年、下一个财年是明年；不是公司的数按自然年。事件的观点写清到哪一天看它处在哪一格。

每个候选观点另填一把键，让代码判断两条观点是不是同一个量：
- measure：从清单里选最贴的量。公司的数：total_revenue、segment_revenue、product_revenue、gross_margin、operating_margin、operating_expense_growth、total_expenses、operating_loss、tax_rate、capex、shipments_or_capacity、run_rate、design_wins；事件：event；世界的数：spend_total、financing_amount、price、capacity、growth_rate、policy_event；都不是：other。
- scope：量的实际限定范围；分部、产品、群体或事件对象。参考名称含义相同时沿用，没有限定写空字符串。
- period_start / period_end：这个量覆盖的起止日（ISO）。财年按财年说明换算；自然年 2026 = 2026-01-01 到 2026-12-31；事件写提出当年年初到到期日。
- basis：GAAP、non_GAAP 或 n/a。unit：USD、percent、count、GW、MW、TWD、multiple 或 n/a。event_type：measure 是 event 或 policy_event 时选 launch、shipment、licence、approval、deal_close、deployment、other，否则 n/a。
- 梯子每格另写 lo、hi：这一格数值区间的下界（含）和上界（不含），用 unit 的单位（美元写完整数字，百分比写 73 不写 0.73）；最低格 lo 写 null，最高格 hi 写 null；是/否两格都写 null。


同时把候选观点归入所谈的持续业务过程，例如产品推出、投资项目或政策过程；公司相同不够。
可以复用下面展示的研究主线编号，也可以在 threads 声明有名称和范围的新主线；在候选的 thread_ids 引用。
同一过程的不同问题可以共用主线，一个问题也可以属于多条。归组不合并问题，也不表示因果或依赖。
只更新已有观点的证据时不用再造候选或主线。

【这一类是什么、怎么读】T7。新闻：媒体发的报道。官方或公司确认的算发生的事；「知情人士称」「据报道」算传闻；文中引用的公司或官员的话算当事人说的；记者自己的判断算第三方看法。

【讲的是谁】这条信息的相关对象：NVDA。候选观点讲的是公司时，object 写股票代码；讲的是主题时，从下面名单里挑一个写编号，名单里没有的写清是什么事：
  - chip-export-controls：芯片出口管制
  - ai-capex：AI 资本开支
  - custom-silicon：云厂商自研芯片
  - semiconductor-cycle：半导体周期
  - fed-policy-rate：美联储政策利率
  - us-inflation：美国通胀
  - us-recession-risk：美国衰退风险
  - us-china-tariffs：中美关税
  - taiwan-strait：台海局势
  - middle-east-conflict：中东冲突与油价
  - russia-ukraine-war：俄乌战争
  - supply-chain-shift：供应链转移与航运
财年说明（数字观点的年份和到期日按这个算）：
NVDA 的财年在 1 月结束，财年按结束的那一年命名：FY2027 从 2026-02 到 2027-01，发布日 2026-07-28 落在 FY2027，所以今年是 FY2027，明年是 FY2028；FY2027 的全年数在 2027-02 前后的年报里公布，到期日按那天写。

【这一类要读出什么】发生了什么事、什么时候、涉及谁；说法从哪来，原始来源是谁、哪天说的；引用的数字。

【研究参考】已有的量和范围（measure[scope](event_type)）。含义相同可用现有名称；清单外的重要问题照常提出，保留实际范围：
  - NVDA：total_revenue；segment_revenue；gross_margin；operating_margin；operating_expense_growth；tax_rate；capex；product_revenue[Blackwell+Rubin]；product_revenue[Vera]；shipments_or_capacity[Rubin]；event[Rubin](shipment)；event[Rubin](launch)；event[H20/H200 China](licence)；event[SK Telecom AI factory](deployment)

【这些对象已有的观点】证据连到这些观点上，用它们的编号；它们管不到的才写候选观点：
  - v1（NVDA，看的是「Nvidia 是否为 OpenAI 数据中心租赁和债务融资提供约 2500 亿美元担保」，到期 2027-07-26）：截至 2027-07-26，Nvidia 是否已为 OpenAI 数据中心租赁和债务融资提供约 2500 亿美元担保？
  - v2（NVDA，看的是「Nvidia 是否为 OpenAI 至多 3500 亿美元的芯片采购提供融资」，到期 2027-07-26）：截至 2027-07-26，Nvidia 是否已为 OpenAI 至多 3500 亿美元的芯片采购提供融资？

Apple retakes world's most valuable company as AI doubts knock Nvidia
The iPhone maker climbed to a record $4.95 trillion valuation after investors questioned whether the AI infrastructure boom can deliver the returns markets have priced in.
Shir Reiter
11:44, 28.07.26
Apple has reclaimed the title of the world's most valuable company, overtaking Nvidia as investors grow increasingly cautious about the artificial intelligence investment boom.
Apple's shares rose 1.2% on Monday, lifting the iPhone maker's market capitalization to a record $4.95 trillion. Nvidia, meanwhile, fell 5%, reducing its market value to $4.78 trillion, after Bloomberg reported that the cost of insuring the chipmaker's debt against default had risen by a record amount amid concerns over its growing commitments to AI infrastructure investments.
1 View gallery
Nvidia
( Reuters//Dado Ruvic )
The changing of the guard reflects a broader shift in investor sentiment. After driving the market higher for more than two years, AI-related stocks are facing increased scrutiny as investors question whether the enormous spending on AI infrastructure will ultimately generate adequate returns.
Nvidia, widely viewed as the biggest beneficiary of the AI investment boom, had held the title of the world's most valuable company for more than a year after surpassing Microsoft in June 2025. But its valuation has compressed in recent months. The company now trades at a forward price-to-earnings multiple of 18.2, down from 25.5 at the beginning of the year.
Apple, by contrast, has emerged as one of the market's biggest winners. According to Dow Jones Market Data, its shares have outperformed the Nasdaq 100 by 23 percentage points since the beginning of July and are on track for their strongest month relative to the index since 2005.
As spending on AI infrastructure continues to accelerate, investors are increasingly focused on whether those investments will produce meaningful financial returns.
Last week, Alphabet raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast, and investors expect other technology giants to follow suit.
Concerns intensified after the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia is in talks to provide $250 billion in financing to OpenAI as part of a data center project in Ohio. According to Jefferies, investors view the proposed arrangement as a prominent example of "circular financing," in which financing provided by a supplier ultimately helps generate demand for its own products.

Nvidia also came under pressure after the IPO of Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT triggered a sharp selloff across the semiconductor sector. Investors fear a new Chinese competitor could erode the pricing power of the industry's three dominant memory manufacturers, Micron, Samsung and SK Hynix.
Reports that Apple is considering purchasing DRAM chips from CXMT to help address the global memory shortage added to concerns over increasing competitive pressure.
Apple has steadily gained ground throughout 2026. Its shares have climbed 24% since the beginning of the year, compared with just 4% for Nvidia. Since the start of July alone, Apple has gained 16%, putting the stock on track for its strongest monthly performance in four years.
The company's rise has come despite a global memory shortage that forced it to raise prices for some Macs and iPads. At the same time, iPhone demand has remained resilient. According to Bernstein analyst Stacy Rasgon, Apple's global smartphone market share has increased to 20%, up from 17% a year earlier.
Unlike most of the so-called "Magnificent Seven," Apple has largely resisted dramatically increasing its capital expenditures on AI infrastructure, opting instead to rent computing capacity rather than build large-scale in-house infrastructure.
Although the company was initially criticized for lacking a clear AI strategy, investors now appear to view that restraint as an advantage. All six of the other Magnificent Seven companies are currently trading at least 15% below their peak share prices.
Apple is scheduled to report fiscal third-quarter results on Thursday. Investors will be watching closely for the company's first detailed assessment of how the global memory chip shortage, driven largely by AI demand, has affected its business.
